en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya Kuṭajapupphiyavagga, Chapter 8, Number 8 [The Elder] Tikaṇṇipupphiya once offered a *tikaṇṇi* flower to the Buddha Vipassī. Because of that root of merit, he was reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand world-ages. Having passed away from there, he was reborn in the human world. There, he was born into a wealthy family and became known as Tikaṇṇipupphiya. When the Blessed One Kassapa appeared in the world, he went forth into homelessness under him. Having practiced the holy life, at the end of his life he was reborn in the Brahma-world. From there, having passed away, he was reborn in the human world. There, he was born into a wealthy family and became known as Tikaṇṇipupphiya. When the Blessed One Gotama appeared in the world, he went forth into homelessness under him. Having attained arahantship, he lived for eighty years. Then, having performed the *thūlōkāsana* (the posture of the final passing), he attained parinibbāna. Thus, the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya has completed his task; he has done what was to be done and has laid down the burden. He has reached his own goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through right knowledge. This is the account of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya. The *Apadāna* of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya is concluded. The *Kuṭajapupphiyavagga*, the eighth chapter, is concluded. The *Therāpadāna* is concluded. May there be well-being. May there be success. “Having become a deva,
honored by apsarases,
I remembered my former karma.”
I recollected the Best of Buddhas.
Having taken a *tikaṇṇi* flower,
I gladdened my own heart.
I offered it to the Buddha Vipassi, the bull among men;
ninety-one aeons ago.
Because I offered this flower in worship,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
In the seventy-third aeon,
there were four supreme and most excellent kings,
endowed with the seven treasures.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya speak these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya.
